items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 4:1
items.html: The line of the Ein Sof, blessed be He, in the first restriction concluded at the point of this world, because there is the discernment that cannot receive His light, may He be blessed, by reason of the restriction made upon it. Therefore the line concluded there, and there concluded the feet of AK, which clothe upon the line of the Ein Sof, blessed be He. And just as the end of the straightness is at the middle point, which is above the point of this world, so the end of the surrounding [lights] of the circles is at the point of this world — except that the matter of up and down does not apply in the circles, and therefore their end is their center. That is, the discernment of the empty void of the circles is at their central point, which is the point of this world. It is thus found that the last circle of the surroundings is the closest of all to the point of this world, and to the underside of the feet of AK. And this last circle of the surroundings is called by the name "the surrounding light that is beneath the feet of the straightness of AK." For after this last circle all the light of the surroundings has concluded, since it surrounds the place of the empty void, which is the point of this world, upon which the feet of AK likewise conclude. Thus it is found that it surrounds also the conclusion of the feet of AK. (Item 3).
